rows.idea: Naive N-1 longest-path BF; no inf/cycle rule
CONTROL: any positive cycle reachable from 1 => inf; does not check cycle can reach N
Filter the graph to vertices that are both reachable from vertex 1 and can reach vertex N, then run Bellman-Ford to detect any positive cycle that can affect the path to N.
Filter the graph to vertices that are both reachable from vertex 1 and can reach vertex N, then use Bellman-Ford on this induced subgraph to find the maximum score or detect a positive cycle.
Run SPFA with negated edge weights from vertex 1, and whenever a vertex is relaxed at least N times, verify via reachability whether it can reach vertex N to declare inf.
Filter the graph to vertices that can reach vertex N via backward BFS, then run Bellman-Ford from vertex 1 for N iterations to find the maximum score or detect reachable positive cycles.

Run Bellman-Ford for N rounds to compute the maximum score, record the distance to vertex N, and then run an additional N rounds to check if vertex N's score continues to strictly increase due to a reachable positive cycle.
Filter the graph to vertices lying on paths from 1 to N using forward and backward BFS, then run Bellman-Ford to detect any positive cycle on the remaining subgraph.

Filter the graph to vertices that both are reachable from vertex 1 and can reach vertex N via two BFS passes, then run Bellman-Ford on the induced subgraph to find the maximum score or detect a positive cycle.

Negate all edge weights to transform the problem into finding the shortest path, then run 2N iterations of Bellman-Ford: if the distance to vertex N strictly decreases between iteration N and 2N, a negative cycle affects N (output inf); otherwise, the answer is -dist[N].
